title: Run My Threads
summary: One setup builds a week plan, then once a day your agent prepares five Threadify-written posts (a thread on six days, one greatest-hit repost, hook-first structures and your CTA level), shows them for one reply, and schedules them only after you say yes.
triggers: prepare my Threads posts every morning for approval
plan my Threads week and prepare each day for approval

inputs.name: one-time setup choices and connected account

outputs.name: daily approval card and schedule receipt

free_capabilities: deterministic weekly planner that checks 35 posts, 6 threads, one greatest hit a day and the CTA count
deterministic hook check on line 1 of every generated post
local casing guard that proves Threadify copy was only lowercased
public Threads playbook and hook template bank
one daily host schedule set up with the host's own controls
paid_capability_stubs: Threadify post generation counts toward the plan's AI generations
model choice depends on the plan: Claude Opus 5.5 when the plan allows it, Gemini as fallback
greatest hits ranking is a paid Threadify feature; without it the slot is generated instead
Auto Plug replies need a plan that includes Auto Plug; otherwise CTAs move to listicle-plug posts

must_show: local and UTC time for each slot
exact final text, threads in full
greatest hit source and stale-fact check
CTA type and exact plug text
Auto Plug and Auto Repost state

instructions: Never write posts yourself when Threadify generation is unavailable; report the exact blocker and manual next step.
When the casing guard fails, present Threadify's original text unchanged.
When a hook check fails, ask Threadify once for a replacement; never hand-edit.
When no greatest hit passes the 60-day and stale-fact checks, generate that slot instead; never rewrite a past post.
When Auto Plug is not echoed back, report it and move future CTAs to listicle-plug posts.
When the host has no durable scheduler, say so and run only when the owner asks.

must_prove: week plan day and CTA count
greatest hit used and byte-identical check
